title: Loving-kindness
line: Goodwill for yourself, for those you love, for strangers and for those you find hard.
intro: Loving-kindness (metta) comes from the Buddha’s teaching but needs no belief at all. You simply wish well: first to yourself, then outward, circle by circle, until it includes everyone.

steps.title: Arrive
steps.text: Breathe gently. Let your shoulders drop.

steps.title: The old words
steps.text: The heart of the Discourse on Loving-kindness. Read it slowly, out loud if you can.

steps.title: Widen the circle
steps.text: Repeat it, and with each repetition think of someone further out: yourself, someone you love, someone you hardly know, someone you find difficult, every being.

steps.title: Notice
steps.prompt: Who was hardest to wish well, and what happened when I tried?

steps.title: Close
steps.text: Rest for a moment in the wish itself.

after: Goodwill grows with use. You can do this in one breath on a bus, or for an hour.
